description:
The in-queue entry, the park record and the receive-entry walk must be guarded by one per-process lock whose scope is fixed now, while a single worker makes it uncontended, so that the multi-worker step inherits a correct boundary. Two hazards define the scope:
- Two senders cannot both consume one park: the lock holder is the only party that may take the park record; the loser finds none and delivers a plain miss. A timer firing takes the same lock and wins or loses the same way; the stale-timer check in Scheduler::wake_expired keeps its role as the fallback.
- reach_receive walks the mailbox then installs the park record (runtime/src/sched.rs:145-165). A delivery between the end of the walk and the install would be probed by nobody. The lock covers the walk and the install together (receiver-side twin of libdispatch's _dispatch_queue_drain_try_unlock failing on DIRTY).

Also: a receiver that exits with un-grafted entries in its in-queue returns every segment to a pool (orphan rule). With one worker a receiver that exits has always drained its in-queue at dispatch, so the only process torn down holding un-grafted gifts is one left parked when the run ends; the fixture uses that case. Pool occupancy is reported by the run-end telemetry event fz.runtime.run_ended (pool_outstanding_before_run, pool_outstanding_after_run, pool_cached_blocks), emitted once on the JIT and interpreter paths after teardown; the AOT path has no telemetry bus. The compiler's own heaps live on the same thread, so the absolute count is never zero; the run's guarantee is before == after, which fixture 00697 asserts. The CLI pin listing events after the execution-ready boundary gains this event.

Interpreter: its park record type lives in the fz crate (IrInterpRuntime.backend_parked), which the runtime crate cannot name, so it stays outside Delivery. The interpreter's probe, timer and delivery paths take the receiver's lock, which guards the pending-match decision and the in-queue; the park map itself is owned by the single interpreter thread.

Tests:
- Unit test on the delivery path: a hit and a timeout for the same park, in either order; exactly one wakes the process, the other finds no park.
- Unit test: a delivery that arrives during the receive-entry critical section is probed after the park is installed (sequencing proven through the lock, not timing).
- Fixture: a receiver that exits while messages are still queued for it leaks nothing (pool occupancy before and after, three paths).

Done when the above pass, the full gate is green, the lock scope is written down in the scheduler agent doc in present tense, and no pin is edited (report). Commit in Why / What changed / Verification form; no co-author trailer.
title: Delivery holds the receiver's queue lock across park, scan and in-queue
